purpose: Describe the exact state shape behind the published benchmark so its ratios are not generalized to arbitrary state.

checkpoint_semantics.state_schema: canonical JSON object with one ordered messages array
checkpoint_semantics.transition: exactly one append_message operation per checkpoint node
checkpoint_semantics.shared_node_rule: parent checkpoint identity and appended message SHA-256 must both match exactly

derivation.input: the frozen evaluation JSONL identified by frozen_evaluation_sha256
derivation.appended_message_bytes: root logical_state_len minus the empty messages wrapper; otherwise child logical_state_len minus parent logical_state_len minus one comma byte
derivation.resulting_state_bytes: the logical_state_len stored and independently verified for each unique checkpoint node

interpretation: The benchmark exercises long append-only persistent sequences whose child state is an exact parent plus one message.
The median appended message is less than one percent of the resulting cumulative state.
Only 166 observed checkpoints reused an exact node across attempts, so the result is not dominated by broad cross-attempt deduplication.
The result does not predict storage for arbitrary full-state blobs, compressed or encrypted snapshots, approximate similarity, or in-place mutation.
